modalLead: Health and the Inbox share one shell now, with a left column listing every filter and its count instead of a second row of tiles saying the same thing above the list. Monitors gets a place of its own in that rail, rows can sit closer together or further apart with one shared setting, and both headers stay put while you scroll.

items.text: A review session can put a link aside for a month. The card offered Re-check, Open, Delete and Skip, so a link that is broken on purpose — a service off for the winter, a host that only answers from another network — had no honest answer. Ignore 30d is that answer: it silences the link everywhere, and the row leaves the session because it has been dealt with.

Health has the same left column as the Inbox. Every filter is a row there with its count, and the tiles that repeated those counts above the list are gone. Score, the trend, the broken count and the report's age sit above the filters as plain readouts. A filter with nothing in it drops out of the list and comes back once it fills.

Monitors is a place of its own in the rail now, not a filter. Opening it swaps the list for the fleet panel — pooled uptime, the worst performers, recent outages — rather than narrowing the list the way the Monitored filter still does. It has its own address, so it is bookmarkable and returns you to the same view on reload.

The rail's Monitors row no longer reads like the Monitored filter above it. They sat one above the other with the same count and near-identical labels, even though one narrows the list and the other opens the fleet panel. It now reads All monitors, matching the panel's own heading.

The header stays put while you scroll. Work through, Rot report, the ⋯ menu and the ℹ explainer stay reachable from anywhere in a long list. The trend chart moved into the ⋯ menu, as Healthy over time.
Health rows can be compact or comfortable, using the setting the Inbox already offered.
Typing in the search box no longer rebuilds the whole view behind your cursor.
Arrow keys can step past the first filter again. A second press used to land back on the row the first one reached.
The title's Smart Why explainer opens by keyboard again.
The rail's Uptime 24h reading is no longer stuck on "0%". It now reads "no data" while nothing has been sampled yet, instead of a number that was never real.
The trend sparkline is back, under the trend figure in the left column. The full chart is still one click away in the ⋯ menu.

The rail's filter rows and summary card have their rounded surface, shadow and hover lift back in the modern layout, and their keyboard focus ring is visible again in both layouts — along with the header actions and the density toggle, which lost the same ring the same way.

The inbox has a left column. The filters moved there as a list with their counts, and This week sits above them as a plain readout. The row of tiles above the list is gone, since it showed the same counts a second time; Snoozed and With note now appear only when there is something in them.
The header stays put while you scroll. It shrinks to a single bar as it sticks, so Triage stays reachable from anywhere in a long list, and the left column sticks with it.

The left column becomes one scrolling line on a narrow screen. The figures move up under the title and the ℹ explainer joins the ⋯ menu, so a phone gets the list instead of four rows of controls above it.
Rows can be compact or comfortable. It is one setting for the whole app rather than one per view.
Typing in the search box no longer rebuilds the whole view behind your cursor.
The site filter no longer sends the hostname you picked to analytics. It reports a fixed marker instead, under the same event name as before.

Clicking a row's domain chip now behaves like every other filter change. It used to leave a stale selection behind and forget the site choice on reload; it now goes through the same path picking it from the list does.

Pressing ? a second time while the finder line is open no longer breaks what you type next. A second press used to add a second finder marker and search for it literally, instead of doing nothing the way a key with no job left should.
The finder line says when you have not set up any finders yet, on a bare ?, with a way straight to Config → Pages & tags & Finders to add one.
Escape no longer throws away a selection while closing a popover. Dismissing the Tags, Checking or date popover with Escape used to clear whatever rows you had ticked underneath it too.
The Checking popover closes when you click away from it, like every other action popover already did.
Typing in the filter box no longer makes your widgets disappear. The clock, the weather and the rest used to vanish the moment you typed the first letter of a bookmark filter.
Long category titles shrink to fit again.
An empty page no longer keeps the previous page's column layout under its "nothing here yet" message.
Custom widgets no longer show stale figures after a manual refresh.
Alt+←/→ and Shift+Alt+←/→ move a category header again on a page you have never dragged on.

The quick-action toolbar and its keys no longer follow you into Config, Inbox and Health. Add, search, commands, finders, recent, help and fold are dashboard-only again, and hide the moment a full-container view opens. The tag-cloud toggle had the same gap and is fixed the same way.

A theme's dark half no longer wears a different backdrop shape than its light half. 111 of the 224 built-in themes had their two variants land on two different backdrop recipes — a diagonal wireframe on one side, a glow from below on the other — when only the colours were meant to change. This changes the look of those 111 dark themes, each now drawn with the shape its light half already had.
